questions.question: Which of the following states of India still uses the ancient bamboo drip irrigation method?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Meghalaya.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Meghalaya** still uses the ancient **bamboo drip irrigation method**, which is a traditional method of irrigation that involves the use of **bamboo pipes** to supply water to crops. 
 
• Meghalaya's **unique topography**, with its hills and valleys, makes it well-suited for this method of irrigation as it allows for the** collection and distribution** of water to different levels of the terrain.
 
• This method is **eco-friendly, cost-effective,** and sustainable as it uses locally available resources and does not require electricity or fuel to operate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Telangana** primarily uses modern irrigation methods such as **sprinkler and drip irrigation. **
 
• **Maharashtra **also primarily uses **modern irrigation methods,** although some farmers may still use traditional methods on a small scale.
 
• **Chhattisgarh** primarily uses** canal irrigation** and **tube wells** for irrigation purposes.
 
• Bamboo drip irrigation is also known as the** "jingkieng ksiar"** method in Meghalaya and has been used for centuries by the** Khasi tribe.**
 
• The bamboo pipes used in this method are **perforated with small holes **to allow water to drip slowly onto the roots of the crops.
 
• Other traditional methods of irrigation used in India include the use of **bullock carts **to draw water from wells, the construction of **earthen embankments** to create ponds and the use of traditional water harvesting structures such as** stepwells and baolis.**

questions.question: The Family Courts (Amendment) Act 2022 has amended the Family Courts Act, 1984. The Act allows ______ to establish Family Courts.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**State Governments.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **State Governments** are allowed to establish **Family Courts** under the **Family Courts (Amendment) Act, of 2022.**
 
• The **Family Courts Act, of 1984 **was enacted to provide for the establishment of Family Courts for **speedy settlement** of family disputes.
 
• The Act applies to all states and Union Territories of India, except** Jammu and Kashmir.**
 
• The **District Courts **are already established under the **Code of Civil Procedure, 1908**, and they do not have the specific mandate of dealing with family disputes.
 
• The **Union Government **does not have the power to establish Family Courts as it is a subject under the State List of the Constitution of India.
 
• The **District Collector** is an administrative officer who is responsible for the collection of **revenue and maintenance of law and order **in the district. 
 
• Therefore, State Governments are the appropriate authority to establish Family Courts as they have the power to make laws on the subject of family disputes under the** State List of the Constitution **of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Family Courts (Amendment) Act, 2022 w**as passed by the Parliament of India on** 17th March 2022.**
 
• The Act was brought in to amend certain provisions of the Family Courts Act, **1984** to make it more effective and efficient.
 
• The Family Courts Act, of 1984 defines family disputes as disputes between** parties to a marriage,** between **parents and children**, or between other relations.
 
• The Act provides for the establishment of **Family Courts **in every city or town with a population of more than 10 lakhs.
 
• The State Governments have the power to establish **Family Courts and appoint judges** for a term of three years.
 
• The judges must have special **knowledge** in matters relating to family disputes.
 
• The Act also provides for the **appointment of counselors **to assist the parties in resolving their disputes amicably.
 
• The establishment of Family Courts has been a significant step towards addressing the issue of **pending cases** in the Indian judicial system.
 
• The Family Courts have been able to provide** speedy and effective justice** to the parties involved in family disputes.

questions.question:
In the context of ecology, the given equation shows the relationship between the size of an area and the number of species present in it. Accordingly, by which letter is the regression coefficient denoted?

log S = log C + Z log A
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Z.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** regression coefficient **in the given equation is denoted by the **letter Z.**
 
• The equation is known as the **species-area relationship** and is used to predict the number of species present in a given area based on its size.
 
• The coefficient Z represents the **slope of the regression line** and measures the **rate** at which the number of **species increases** with** increasing area.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** constant C** represents the intercept of the** regression line **and represents the** number of species** present in a unit area.
 
• **S** represents the** number of species.**
 
• **A** represents the **size of the area.**
 
• In general, there are more plant and animal species on** larger lands** than on smaller ones.
 
• Almost all terrestrial systems that have been investigated, from vast** continental regions** to **island archipelagos,** have shown this link to hold true.

questions.question: Which of the following hypotheses was propounded by Harry Hammond Hess in 1962?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sea floor spreading hypothesis.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Harry Hammond Hess **proposed the **seafloor spreading hypothesis** in **1962**, which explained the mechanism behind continental drift.
 
• This hypothesis suggested that **new oceanic crust **is formed at **mid-ocean ridges** and then moves away from the ridge, carrying the continents with it.
 
• This theory was supported by evidence such as **magnetic anomalies** in the** oceanic crust** and the age of oceanic rocks becoming progressively younger towards the mid-ocean ridges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• According to **Alfred Wegener's theory**, the continents were formerly part of a single supercontinent called **Pangaea,** which means **"all of earth"** in Greek.

 
 
• He proposed that the continents relocated to their present locations when **Pangaea **broke apart a long time ago.
 
• He dubbed** continental drift** his theory.
 
 
 
• The **Gaia hypothesis** was proposed by **James Lovelock** in the **1970s**.
 
 
• It suggests that the Earth is a **self-regulating system** that maintains conditions necessary for life.
 
 
 
• The** geographical cycle hypothesis** was proposed by** William Morris Davis** in the late 19th century.
 
 
• He suggested that landforms were shaped by a cycle of** erosion, transportation, and deposition.**

• Article 43 B was **not** added in 2002.

questions.question: Silicon doped with gallium forms ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is a __**p-type semiconductor.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Silicon **doped with** gallium** forms a** p-type semiconducto**r because gallium is a** trivalent impurity** and replaces some of the silicon atoms in the crystal lattice, creating a** hole** in the valence band.
 
• **P-type semiconductors** have a **majority of holes** as their charge carriers and a smaller number of **electrons,** which are the minority carriers.
 
• **N-type semiconductors,** on the other hand, are doped with a **pentavalent impurity** like phosphorus, which adds an extra electron to the conduction band and creates a **surplus of electrons** as the majority carriers.
 
• **Superconductors **are materials that exhibit **zero electrical resistance **below a certain** temperature, **and **silicon doped with gallium** is not known to exhibit superconductivity.
 
• **Insulators **are materials that do not conduct electricity at all and have a **very high resistance,** which is not the case with **p-type semiconductors.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In a** p-type semiconductor**, the holes in the valence band can move from **one atom to another **and act as **positive charge carriers**, while the electrons in the conduction band are** immobile unless **excited by an external energy source. 
 
• The doping process is a way to intentionally introduce impurities into a **semiconductor crystal** to alter its electrical properties and enable the creation of **p-n junctions**, which are the basis of many **electronic devices.**
 
• Some common **p-type dopants** besides gallium are** boron and aluminum, **while common **n-type dopants** include **arsenic and antimony.**
 
• The properties of a semiconductor depend not only on its doping but also on its** temperature, light exposure**, and other environmental factors that can affect its **carrier concentration, mobility, and recombination.**

questions.question:
Match the following items with respect to money.

 
 

 **List I**
 **List II**
 
 

 i.
 Primary functions
 a.
 Distribution of national income
 
 

 ii.
 Secondary functions
 b.
 Measure of value
 
 

 iii.
 Evils of money
 c.
 Store of value
 
 

 iv.
 Contingent functions
 d.
 Instability of value

options.text: i - d, ii - c, iii - a, iv - b
i - a, ii - d, iii - b, iv - c
i - c, ii - b, iii - a, iv - d
i - b, ii - c, iii - d, iv - a

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**i - b, ii - c, iii - d, iv - a.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **correct option** is primary functions - **b**, secondary functions - **c**, evils of money - **d**, contingent functions - **a.**
 
• Money is an** essential elemen**t of our economy, and it performs several functions that are crucial for the **smooth functioning** of the economy.
 
• The primary function of money is to act as a** medium of exchange**, i.e., it facilitates the exchange of goods and services.
 
 
• Money also acts as a **measure of value**, i.e., it helps in determining the value of goods and services.
 
 
 
• The secondary functions of money include acting as a** store of value**, i.e., it helps in storing the wealth in the form of money.
 
 
• It also acts as a standard of **deferred payments**, i.e., it facilitates the payment of debts in the future.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **evils of money** include **instability of value**, i.e., the value of money keeps fluctuating due to various economic factors.

 
 
• Money can also create **inflation**, i.e., the rise in the general price level of goods and services.
 
 
 
• The contingent functions of money include acting as a means of **distribution of national income**, i.e., it helps in distributing the national income among various sections of the society.
 
 
• Money also acts as a source of **public revenue,** i.e., the government earns revenue by imposing taxes on various economic activities.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a fundamental duty in the Indian Constitution?

options.text: To maintain and protect the sovereignty of the country
To promote the spirit of harmony and brotherhood

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**protection of monuments and heritage sites.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Protecting public property** is a fundamental duty of Indian citizens as it is important for the welfare and development of the society.
 
• Safeguarding the** sovereignty, unity, and integrity** of the country is a fundamental duty of Indian citizens.
 
• Promoting **harmony and brotherhood** among all people of India is a fundamental duty of Indian citizens.
 
• The protection of monuments and heritage sites is** not **listed as a fundamental duty in the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ​__The** fundamental duties** of Indian citizens are listed under **Article 51A** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• There are **11 fundamental duties** listed in the Constitution.
 
• These duties were added by the **42nd Amendment Act **in **1976.**
 
• Fundamental Duties were recommended by the** Swaran Singh Committee in 1976**, and their importance became apparent during the internal emergency of **1975–1977.**

questions.question: During a boom, the deficit of the government will reduce automatically due to ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**increase in tax revenue.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• During a** boom, **people tend to **earn more,** which increases their** taxable income **and, in turn, the government's **tax revenue.**
 
• Hence, the deficit of the government will** be reduced **automatically due to an increase in tax revenue.
 
• As the economy grows during a boom, businesses also tend to earn **more profits,** leading to** higher corporate tax collections** for the government.
 
• During a boom, the government may also earn more from other sources, such as** dividends, royalties, and fees,** which can contribute to reducing the deficit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A **booming economy** also leads to more **employment opportunities**, which reduces the government's expenditure on welfare programs such as **unemployment benefits** and** food assistance.**
 
• A** higher GDP** indicates a larger economy, which can generate more income for the government.
 
 
• However, it is the** increase in tax revenue** that contributes to reducing the deficit, not the GDP itself.
 
 
 
• **A decrease in tax revenue** would lead to an **increase **in the government deficit, not a reduction.
 
• **A Decrease in GDP** would lead to a decline in overall economic activity, resulting in** lower tax collections** and **higher government expenditure**, leading to an **increase in the deficit.**

questions.question: What percentage of the Indian population was estimated to be living below the poverty line in 2011-12?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**21.9%.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **21.9% **of the Indian population was estimated to be living **below the poverty line.**
 
• This means that around** 270 million people **in India were living below the poverty line in** 2011-12**.
 
• The **poverty line in India **is defined as the minimum level of income required to meet basic needs such as **food, clothing, and shelter.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Poverty in India** is a major issue, with a **large population** struggling to meet their basic needs.
 
• The poverty line in India is determined by the **Planning Commission, **which takes into account factors such as the **cost of food, health care, and education.**
 
• The poverty line is different for rural and urban areas in India, with the **rural poverty line** being **lower** than the urban poverty line.
 
• **Poverty reduction** has been a priority for the Indian government, with various schemes and programs aimed at improving the** lives of the poor.**
 
• However, progress has been slow and there is still a long way to go in **addressing the issue of poverty** in India.

questions.question: The Himalayan Mountains act as an effective climatic divide by protecting the subcontinent from:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**cold northern winds.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Himalayan Mountains** are the highest mountain range in the world and act as a **natural barrier** that separates the Indian subcontinent from the rest of Asia.
 
• The mountains act as an effective** climatic divide** by protecting the subcontinent from the** cold northern winds** that blow from the** Tibetan Plateau** and **Central Asia.**
 
• The Himalayas also block the** warm southern winds** that originate from the **Indian Ocean**, preventing them from entering the subcontinent and making the climate cooler and drier.
 
• Cyclonic winds are **not affected** by the Himalayan Mountains and can still enter the subcontinent, causing** heavy rainfall and flooding** in some regions.
 
• **Western disturbances** are weather systems that originate from the** Mediterranean region** and can enter the subcontinent from the northwest, but their impact is reduced by the Himalayan Mountains.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Himalayan Mountains are located in the **northern part of the Indian subcontinent** and stretch over **2,400 km** from **Afghanistan to Myanmar.**
 
• The mountains are home to some of the highest peaks in the world, including **Mount Everest,** which is the highest peak at 8,848 meters.
 
• The Himalayas are also the source of many major rivers in** South Asia,** including the** Ganges, Brahmaputra, and Indus rivers.**
 
• **Cyclonic winds **are **low-pressure systems** that form over warm ocean waters and can cause** heavy rainfall and strong winds **when they make landfall.
 
 
• They are common in the** Bay of Bengal** and the** Arabian Sea.**
 
 
 
• Western disturbances are weather systems that **bring rain and snow **to the western Himalayan region from November to April.
 
 
• They are important for** agriculture and water supply** in the region.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT one of the common goals of five-year plans?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Globalisation.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• The **five-year plans** were introduced in India in **1951** to accelerate the pace of** economic growth and development.**
 
• **Self-reliance, modernization, growth, and equity** are the four common goals of five-year plans.
 
• Self-reliance aims to **reduce dependence **on foreign aid and promote domestic resources.
 
• Modernization aims to promote** industrialization, technological advancement,** and **infrastructure development**.
 
• Growth aims to increase the **national income **and improve the **living standards **of the people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Globalization** refers to the integration of **economies, cultures, and societies **across the world.
 
• It is not a common goal of **five-year plans** as it emerged as a concept in the **1990s.**
 
• **Self-reliance** is an important concept that has been emphasized in India's** economic policies** since independence.
 
 
• It aims to promote indigenous** industries, reduce imports, and encourage exports.**
 
 
 
• **Modernization** is critical for achieving **sustainable economic growth** and **development**.
 
 
• It includes the adoption of new **technologies,** **modernizing infrastructure**, and improving the **quality of education** and healthcare.
 
 
 
• **Growth **is an essential goal of **economic development** as it helps to reduce **poverty, unemployment, and inequality**.
 
 
• However, growth must be **inclusive and sustainable** to benefit all sections of society.

questions.question: The novel Self-Help Group Bank Linkage Program (SHG-BLP) project which grew into a dominant micro finance model, was piloted by ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**NABARD.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **NABARD **was the organization that piloted the** Self-Help Group Bank Linkage Program** (SHG-BLP) project in India.
 
• NABARD came into existence on **12 July 1982 **by transferring the agricultural credit functions of RBI and refinance functions of the then **Agricultural Refinance and Development Corporation (ARDC)**.
 
• It was dedicated to the service of the nation by the late **Prime Minister Smt. Indira Gandhi on 05 November 1982.**
 
• The SHG-BLP project is a** microfinance model **that involves linking **self-help groups of women **in rural areas with formal financial institutions like banks, to provide them with access to **credit and financial services.**
 
• Full form of NABARD is the **National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Microfinance institutions** (MFIs) are organizations that provide financial services to** low-income individuals or groups **who do not have access to traditional banking services.

 
 
• Any loan amount in India** under one lakh rupees** is regarded as a **microloan.**
 
 
 
• **The Ministry of Finance, Government of India**, has control over the** Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India**, which is a statutory entity.
 
 
• Its job is to** license and oversee** the insurance and reinsurance sectors in India.
 
 
 
• Under the administrative purview of the **Ministry of Finance in the Government of India**, the **Securities and Exchange Board of India **(SEBI) is the regulatory authority for the securities and commodities market in India.
 
 
• SEBI was founded on **April 12, 1988,** as an executive body, and on **January 30, 1992, the SEBI Act, 1992**, granted it legislative authority.
